approval_basis: Independent review outside the release automation; the Gate binding was resolved once at this boundary through the release module's own gate builder, with no routine or repeated digest checking. Adoption and drift: the manifest goes from 34 to 35 cases, the single addition is reservation-owned-store-accepted expecting only RESIDENCY_BOUND, nothing was removed, and the previously reviewed 34 cases show zero expectation drift - no finding-code list changed and no accepted or lowering_eligible disposition moved. The source set gains exactly the new Schedule for 51 entries and contains no test path. The Compiler's own check_corpus recomputed the Gate at 35 cases with no mismatched case. TinyGEMM2 shows no regression: tinygemm2-r31-accepted still matches as accepted and lowering-eligible with only RESIDENCY_BOUND, and tinygemm2-r31-reduction-drift still matches as refused with REDUCE_SUM_SEMANTICS. This slice adds no IR vocabulary at all; a mechanical comparison against HEAD shows zero enum members added or removed, so it is verifier admission plus one Corpus case. Ownership semantics reviewed adversarially. All nine STORE_INDEX ownership codes now carry a minimal falsifier, including the two added since the previous review. STORE_INDEX_RESERVATION_FORM was confirmed reachable through three independent near misses: a single runtime coordinate, a runtime coordinate placed after a dimension index, and three runtime coordinates. STORE_INDEX_RESERVATION_ROLE was verified to be a distinct fact rather than a synonym of the general race rule: with two roles, a well-formed named barrier, and every cross-role producer signalling that handshake, OP_CROSS_ROLE_RACE is suppressed and STORE_INDEX_RESERVATION_ROLE fires alone, stating that the atomic result is register-resident and a barrier cannot move it between roles. Without this rule that Schedule would have passed the ownership proof while asking the lowering to do something it cannot. The earlier loop hazard remains owned by STORE_INDEX_RESERVATION_LOOP rather than by a backend position refusal, an unrelated loop containing neither operation stays legal, and five constructed conflict attacks - a second atomic mutating the state target, clobbering either coordinate between reservation and store, two stores sharing one reservation, and two atomics writing one position - all remain refused. The premises the proof borrows are declared rather than assumed: ADR 0036 names the existing one-writer Buffer invariant as what proves no second operation mutates the state target, delegates ordering and cross-role dataflow to the general rules while stating that a second store-specific dependency rule would duplicate that authority, and records that the Schedule does not constrain the caller's initial state values, so wrap or out-of-capacity positions are dropped by the store mask rather than creating a conflicting write. The observation oracle declares its narrower all-reservations-fit domain before launch and refuses anything outside it, which is exercised by a failure-capable test, while the position upper bound is carried by a generated-source assertion. That split keeps the exact-set oracle exact instead of folding a partial-capacity subset into it. The 88 currently failing suite items were classified line by line, 176 error lines with none outside the pending-release class: the released v27 lock refusing the current manifest, and the stale Gate report and approval this file replaces. Not in scope of this approval: ADR 0036 remains proposed and its fifth acceptance item, one frozen zero-retry brokered B200 correctness observation, has not been made; the runtime behaviour of the position upper bound is asserted in generated source but never executed, which the ADR declares as needing a separate runtime extent relation. This approves the compiler-side ownership slice only, claims no complete KDA-version coverage and authorizes no performance claim.
